parsed.explanation: Documented, enforced Article 120 regime is used by police against trans women through arbitrary detention, prosecution, extortion and forced examinations amounting to torture, with impunity and no legal protection. Once outed, a visitor faces detention, bribery/coerced informing, possible imprisonment up to 3 years, and custodial ill-treatment, with official hostility and unregistrable LGBTI organisations leaving no remedy. Entry, facilities and care are undocumented, not safe. This is state-tolerated/directed targeting well below unremedied-exclusion cases, but short of documented routine presentation convictions and custody sexual assault at 0.15, and worse than raid/extortion cases at 0.25.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police target trans women with arbitrary detention/prosecution; forced examinations amount to torture; custody ill-treatment and impunity documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No protection documented; arrests require bribes for release or coerced informing.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Outing can trigger detention under Article 120, then extortion, forced examination, imprisonment or informant coercion.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Article 120, up to 3 years, prosecuted 2009-2023; police routine intimidation, violence, exploitation of trans people; constitution omits sexual orientation; official hostility.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No anti-discrimination protection documented; LGBTI organisations cannot register.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Sexuality law is secondary in principle but dossier documents it as active police lever against trans women, weighing accordingly.

minors_guardians.interaction: No age-specific rule documented; guardian/child face same general outing/detention/extortion exposure if identified at checkpoints, hotels or police stops, which is not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Routine police intimidation, violence and exploitation; societal harassment continues; rural taboos drive discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police are perpetrators, not protectors; impunity for ill-treatment persists; no legal recourse documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victim reporting risks arrest/extortion under the same criminal framework.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No effective remedy documented; self-censorship narrows local information; most recent prosecution 2023, absence of later case is not evidence of cessation.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Entry, facilities, care, document-marker and trans-specific violence rates remain unknown and are not treated as safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: police arrest gender-nonconforming people under morality/sexuality law, detain, extort, custody abuse, little recourse. This dossier lacks documented routine visitor raids and custody sexual assault, and bribe-release is documented, so slightly higher than 0.15.

Lower: both have police raids/stops, payment for release, custody harassment and no remedy. This dossier adds forced examinations amounting to torture, routine police violence per multiple reports, and enforced imprisonment up to 3 years, so below 0.25.

Materially lower: 0.35 has no identity offence, polite society and only universal facility exclusion with rejected complaints. Here there is active criminalisation used against trans women, detention, torture and extortion, a far more severe post-outing regime.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is nationally uniform: an enforced sexuality offence provides police a detention/extortion lever specifically documented against trans women, compounded by torture in forced examinations, impunity, official hostility and no registrable community or legal recourse. Benefits of passing or paying do not rate. Undocumented border, facility and care axes cannot mitigate. Interacting stages—outing, police stop, bribe/coercion, forced examination, detention—produce severe, state-implicated consequences, placing the jurisdiction at the severe/high-risk boundary.
